claims.text: The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Asymmetric XRD peaks in the initial alloy indicate compositional micro-segregation between dendritic cores and interdendritic regions.
The initial alloy has room-temperature fracture strain significantly below theoretical predictions.
Approximately 4 at.% Cr is added to the Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr drives formation of a complex multicomponent Laves phase.
The Cr-induced Laves phase is of the C14 or C15 structure type.
The Laves phase has a volume fraction of approximately 4%.
The Laves phase is located primarily in interdendritic regions.
A 1200°C, 24 h homogenization treatment permits Laves-phase precipitation without completely dissolving it.
A cooling rate favoring interdendritic segregation preserves the proposed Laves-phase distribution.
The Laves phase forms a reticulated, interconnected network.
The interconnected brittle Laves network impedes crack extension by deflecting cracks onto phase boundaries and producing predominantly intergranular propagation.
Triple junctions in the Laves network create stress concentrations that promote early void nucleation and coalescence.
Cr solute causes substantial lattice distortion and contraction of the BCC matrix through atomic-size mismatch.
Cr-induced lattice distortion increases Peierls stress and solid-solution hardening.
The combined hardening raises yield strength but reduces strain-hardening capacity and promotes premature failure.
The Cr-containing alloy will exhibit a measurable contraction of the BCC lattice parameter relative to the Cr-free baseline.
The Cr-containing alloy will exhibit a distinct secondary phase identifiable as Laves by XRD and TEM.
The Cr-containing alloy's room-temperature fracture strain will remain low or decrease relative to the Cr-free baseline.
A BCC lattice-parameter contraction of at least 0.05% is required, while no contraction falsifies the proposed Cr-induced distortion mechanism.
